function.name: build
function.description: Run a JavaScript program against the shared voxel world. The program can read and write blocks through the mc API. Applied atomically: if it throws, nothing changes — you may throw deliberately to abandon a program you realize is wrong mid-write, then send a corrected one. mc.log output collected before the throw is still returned. When the program changes the world, the result's minecraft field is Minecraft's verdict on the whole blueprint placed fresh and run settle_ticks ticks (default 210, at most ⟦simulationTicks⟧): how many block ids it removed, added or replaced against your blueprint, with example positions, and the ticks it ran. mc.settled(x, y, z) in a program reads that verdict for one position, for the world as it was when the program started (so not this program's own edits): {id, states}, or null for air, at mc.get's coordinates; mc.settledTicks is the ticks that verdict ran.

summary.description: Very short human-readable label for this step, e.g. "Build the house shell".

program.description: JavaScript source. Must assign a synchronous function to module.exports, which receives the mc API object.

settle_ticks.description: Ticks Minecraft runs on the whole blueprint for the result's minecraft field when the program changes the world (default 210: overworld lava moves a step every 30 ticks, so its 7 steps take 210). 0 is the blueprint as placed. Longer settles take longer to run.
